      1 Executive summary#

      The Northwind Bank CRM platform is the bank's system of engagement for retail and business customers. Designed and built by Acme Integrators on Salesforce, it supports two populations, each in a dedicated console application:

      • the branch network (advisors and branch managers) in the « Branch Console », to manage customers, leads and loan applications;
      • the contact center (agents and their manager) in the « Contact Center » console, to qualify leads and record contact attempts.

      Customers interact indirectly through the mobile banking app, which creates leads through an inbound API.

      The solution relies on four Salesforce foundations, complemented by specific developments:

      • Sales Cloud carries the lead and opportunity lifecycle, from the first contact to the loan;
      • Financial Services Cloud provides the financial account model that loan applications refer to;
      • OmniStudio guides the loan intake journey;
      • Platform Events decouple the loan decision from its follow-up actions.
      2Lightning applications 4Custom business objects 12Apex application classes, 5 test classes 4Lightning Web Components 1 / 1OmniScripts / Integration Procedures (active) 3Active flows 5Custom Metadata records (2 types) 6Connected systems

      1.1 Business capabilities covered#

      Domain Main capabilities
      Customer knowledge Customer record with live positions from the core banking system (Customer 360), segment kept in sync every night
      Leads Leads from the mobile app, the branches and the contact center; default branch assignment; scoring at creation
      Loan applications Intake guided by an OmniScript, automatic scoring from configurable rules, decision, document archiving
      Customer notifications SMS reminders for missing documents, follow-up tasks when a status changes
      Contact center Lead queue, contact attempts and their outcome
      Steering Loan reports by status and by branch, loan pipeline dashboard
      Security Single sign-on for employees, persona-based permission set groups, role hierarchy following the network

      1.2 Key achievements#

      Configurable loan scoring

      The score of each loan application is computed by LoanScoringService from rules stored as ScoringRule__mdt records. A new criterion or a new weight is a configuration change: no code, no deployment window.

      Live Customer 360

      Accounts, cards and loans are read in real time from the core banking system through a named credential (NWB_CoreBanking). No position is copied into Salesforce, so advisors always see the figures of the system of record.

      Event-driven loan follow-up

      Every status change of a loan application publishes a LoanStatusChange__e event. Follow-up tasks, notifications and archiving subscribe to it, so new reactions are added without touching the trigger.

      Secure by design integrations

      All calls go through named and external credentials; the inbound lead API runs in user mode; employees log in once through the corporate identity provider, with users created by a registration handler.

      1.3 Architecture principles applied#

      1. Standard first: Sales Cloud objects, Financial Services Cloud accounts, OmniStudio journeys, queues and platform events are used before any specific development.
      2. The core banking system stays the master of customers and positions: Salesforce reads them live and keeps only what the relationship needs.
      3. Configuration in Custom Metadata: scoring rules and integration timeouts are records, changed without code.
      4. One trigger per object, delegating to a handler class; services and selectors separate business logic from data access.
      5. Asynchronous for anything slow: archiving, SMS and nightly synchronisation run outside the user transaction.
      6. Credentials outside the code: every endpoint is a named credential; authentication is held by external credentials.

      2 Purpose, scope and references#

      2.1 Purpose of the document#

      This document describes the technical architecture of the Northwind Bank CRM platform as implemented. It is the reference for:

      • the understanding of the solution by the bank's teams;
      • run, corrective and evolutive maintenance;
      • architecture and security reviews;
      • knowledge transfer between Acme Integrators, Northwind Bank and its partners.

      It is written for architects, application owners, operations and security teams, and the developers who will make the platform evolve.

      3 Context and vision#

      3.1 Business drivers#

      • Give every advisor a complete and current view of the customer, without leaving the CRM.
      • Turn every contact — branch, contact center, mobile app — into a qualified lead handled by the right branch.
      • Shorten the time from loan request to decision, with a score computed the same way everywhere.
      • Keep customers informed at each step of their loan application.
      • Steer the loan pipeline by status and by branch.

      3.2 Actors and user populations#

      Population Application Main activities
      Branch advisors « Branch Console » Customer 360, leads of the branch, loan applications, contact attempts
      Branch managers « Branch Console » Same as advisors, plus branch management and review of submitted loan applications
      Contact center agents « Contact Center » Lead qualification from the contact center queue, contact attempts
      Mobile app customers Mobile banking app Request a call back or a loan: a lead is created through the API

      4 General architecture#

      4.1 Context view#

      Actors: users, populations, channels Salesforce components Systems outside the CRM Data: objects, metadata, reference data

      Users. Employees reach the platform through two Lightning console applications and log in with the corporate identity provider. Customers never log in to Salesforce: the mobile banking app calls an Apex REST service on their behalf.

      Salesforce. The organization combines Sales Cloud objects, the financial account model of Financial Services Cloud, an OmniStudio journey for loan intake and platform events for the loan follow-up. Specific objects hold branches, loan applications, loan documents and contact attempts.

      Connected systems. The core banking system is read in real time and feeds the nightly customer synchronisation; the SMS gateway sends reminders; the document store archives the documents of decided loan applications; the maps provider serves map tiles to the console.

      4.2 Salesforce foundation and products#

      Product Evidence in the metadata
      Sales Cloud object Opportunity, object Lead
      Financial Services Cloud namespace FinServ
      OmniStudio dedicated metadata
      Platform Events / Change Data Capture dedicated metadata
      Product Use in the solution
      Sales Cloud Leads, conversion, opportunities linked to loan applications
      Financial Services Cloud Financial account model referenced by loan applications (LoanApplication__c.FinancialAccount__c)
      OmniStudio Guided loan intake (OmniScript), server-side retrieval of positions (Integration Procedure), loan data extraction (Data Mapper)
      Platform Events Decoupling of the loan status change from its consequences

      Everything else — branches, loan applications, documents, scoring, Customer 360 — is specific and documented in chapters 6 to 9.

      4.3 Logical architecture in layers#

      Layer Components Responsibility
      Presentation Console applications, Lightning pages, LWC, OmniScript Show information and guide the user; no heavy business rule in the browser
      Orchestration Flows, Integration Procedure, Data Mapper Chain the steps of a process; declarative automation
      Apex services Triggers and handlers, controllers, services, selectors, asynchronous jobs Business rules, data access, integrations, volume processing
      Data Standard and industry objects, specific objects, Custom Metadata Business data and configuration
      Integration Named and external credentials, Apex REST, connected app Isolate and secure the exchanges with the bank's systems

      4.4 Design principles#

      • Standard first: standard objects, queues, record types, platform events and OmniStudio before custom code.
      • Configuration over code: business parameters in Custom Metadata (ScoringRule__mdt, IntegrationSetting__mdt).
      • Bulk-safe: triggers process lists, the customer synchronisation (CustomerSyncBatch, designed to run nightly) works in batches of 50 records.
      • Secure server-side: controllers run with sharing and query in user mode; the inbound API inserts records as the calling user.
      • Loose coupling: the trigger publishes an event; subscribers react independently.

      5 Functional architecture and business processes#

      5.1 Functional domains#

      Domain Main objects Main components Section
      Leads and qualification Lead, ContactAttempt__c LeadApiResource, LeadTrigger, Lead_Assign_Branch § 5.2
      Loan applications LoanApplication__c, LoanDocument__c NWB_LoanIntake_English_1, LoanApplicationTrigger, LoanScoringService § 5.3
      Customer 360 Account customer360, Customer360Controller, CoreBankingClient § 5.4
      Notifications LoanStatusChange__e Loan_Status_Notification, Loan_Document_Reminder, SmsNotificationService § 5.5
      Contact center Lead, ContactAttempt__c Queue Contact_Center_Leads, « Contact Center » console § 5.6

      5.2 Leads and qualification#

      Leads come from three channels: the mobile banking app, the branches and the contact center.

      • The mobile app calls the Apex REST service LeadApiResource (/leads/v1/*). The lead is inserted in user mode with its channel (Channel__c).
      • At creation, LeadTrigger delegates to LeadTriggerHandler, which initialises the score (Score__c).
      • The record-triggered flow Lead_Assign_Branch then assigns the lead to its branch (Branch__c).
      • Leads waiting for the contact center are owned by the queue Contact_Center_Leads.
      • A converted lead can no longer change status: the validation rule Lead_Locked_When_Converted enforces it.

      5.3 Loan applications#

      A loan application (LoanApplication__c) is created from the customer record (quick action Account.New_Loan_Application), from the « New loan » tab (loanWizard) or through the guided OmniScript NWB_LoanIntake_English_1. Its record type distinguishes consumer loans from mortgages.

      • Scoring. Before each save, LoanApplicationTriggerHandler asks LoanScoringService to compute Score__c from the ScoringRule__mdt rules.
      • Review. Submitted applications are shared in read-only mode with the branch managers (sharing rule Share_Submitted_With_Review_Team); the queue Loan_Review holds the applications waiting for a reviewer.
      • Decision. Each status change publishes a LoanStatusChange__e event. When the status becomes « Approved » or « Rejected », the documents are archived by DocumentArchiveQueueable.
      • Documents. Each document is a LoanDocument__c record, child of its application (master-detail), with its archive identifier (ArchiveId__c).
      Acme Integrators contribution

      Scoring rules are data, not code: the business team adjusts weights and criteria in ScoringRule__mdt without a release.

      5.4 Customer 360#

      On the customer record page (Account_Record_Page), the customer360 component displays the customer's positions read live from the core banking system:

      1. the component calls Customer360Controller.getPositions through a cached wire adapter;
      2. the controller reads the customer number (NWB_CustomerNumber__c) in user mode;
      3. CoreBankingClient calls the core banking API through the named credential NWB_CoreBanking;
      4. each position is rendered by positionTile.

      CustomerSyncBatch, designed to run each night once scheduled, refreshes the customer segment (Segment__c) from the same API.

      5.5 Notifications#

      • Status change. The flow Loan_Status_Notification subscribes to LoanStatusChange__e and creates a follow-up task for the owner.
      • Missing documents. The scheduled flow Loan_Document_Reminder runs daily on loan applications and calls the invocable action of SmsNotificationService, which sends the SMS through the SMS gateway asynchronously.

      5.6 Contact center#

      Agents work in the « Contact Center » console on the leads of the queue Contact_Center_Leads. Each call is recorded as a contact attempt (ContactAttempt__c) linked to the lead or the customer, with its outcome (Outcome__c).

      6 Data architecture#

      6.1 Modeling principles#

      • Standard objects carry the relationship: Account for customers (retail and business record types), Lead, Opportunity.
      • Financial accounts follow the Financial Services Cloud model; loan applications refer to them.
      • Specific objects exist only for what the standard does not cover: branches, loan applications and their documents, contact attempts.
      • Every record fed by or sent to another system carries an external ID used as matching key.
      • Relationships are lookups, except the documents of a loan application (master-detail: they live and die with it).
      • Business parameters are Custom Metadata records.

      6.2 Overview#

      The customer (Account) is the centre of the model: its branch, its loan applications, its leads and its contact attempts hang off it. The branch (Branch__c) owns customers and leads by default. A loan application gathers its documents and may be linked to an opportunity and to a financial account.

      6.3 Objects by domain#

      6.3.1 Customers and branches#

      Object Role Key fields
      Account Customer (retail or business) NWB_CustomerNumber__c (core banking key), Segment__c, Branch__c, Advisor__c

      LoanDocument__c Document of an application LoanApplication__c (master), DocumentType__c, ArchiveId__c

      Object Use

      The rest of the Financial Services Cloud model is not referenced by the specific metadata.

      6.5 External IDs and integration keys#

      Object Field
      Account NWB_CustomerNumber__c
      Branch__c BranchCode__c
      LoanApplication__c CoreBankingId__c
      LoanDocument__c ArchiveId__c
      • NWB_CustomerNumber__c and CoreBankingId__c are the keys of the core banking system, used by the nightly synchronisation and by the Customer 360 calls.
      • BranchCode__c identifies a branch in the bank's referential.
      • ArchiveId__c is the identifier returned by the document store.

      6.6 Record types and business processes#

      Object Record types
      Account Business_Customer, Retail_Customer
      LoanApplication__c Consumer_Loan, Mortgage

      Customer record types separate retail and business customers (different page layouts and segments). Loan record types separate consumer loans and mortgages, which follow different scoring rules and documents.

      6.7 Configuration in Custom Metadata#

      Type Records
      IntegrationSetting__mdt 2
      ScoringRule__mdt 3
      Type What it configures
      ScoringRule__mdt Criteria and weights of the loan score (Criterion__c, Weight__c)
      IntegrationSetting__mdt Timeouts of the outbound integrations (TimeoutMs__c)

      6.8 Platform events and change data capture#

      API name Label
      LoanStatusChange__e Loan status change

      LoanStatusChange__e carries the loan application identifier and its new status. It is published by LoanApplicationTriggerHandler and consumed by the flow Loan_Status_Notification. No change data capture entity is selected.

      6.9 Files and documents#

      The documents of a loan application are described by LoanDocument__c records; their content is archived in the document store once the application is decided, and the archive identifier is kept on the record.

      6.10 Data lifecycle#

      Field history tracking is enabled on the specific objects. No archiving or purge policy is configured in Salesforce for loan applications and contact attempts: the retention rules are to be confirmed with the bank.

      7 Application architecture#

      7.1 Apex code architecture#

      Nature Count
      Batch 1
      Queueable 1
      Schedulable 1
      @future 1
      REST 1
      Invocable 1
      LWC/Aura controller 2
      Callout 3
      SSO registration handler 1
      Global 2

      7.1.1 Design principles#

      • One trigger per object, with no logic in the trigger body: each trigger calls the run() method of its handler.
      • Business rules live in services (LoanScoringService), data access in selectors (LoanApplicationSelector), external calls in clients (CoreBankingClient).
      • Code processes lists of records, never one record at a time.
      • 8 classes declare with sharing; queries from user-facing code run WITH USER_MODE.

      7.1.2 Layers and conventions#

      Layer Convention Examples
      Trigger handlers <Object>TriggerHandler LoanApplicationTriggerHandler, LeadTriggerHandler
      Services <Domain>Service LoanScoringService, SmsNotificationService
      Selectors <Object>Selector LoanApplicationSelector
      Controllers <Component>Controller Customer360Controller
      Integration clients <System>Client CoreBankingClient
      Asynchronous jobs *Batch, *Queueable CustomerSyncBatch, DocumentArchiveQueueable
      Exposed services *Resource LeadApiResource

      7.1.3 Classes by functional domain#

      Domain Main classes Role
      Loans LoanApplicationTriggerHandler, LoanScoringService, LoanApplicationSelector, DocumentArchiveQueueable Scoring, events, archiving
      Customer 360 Customer360Controller, CoreBankingClient, CustomerSyncBatch Live positions, nightly synchronisation
      Leads LeadApiResource, LeadTriggerHandler Inbound API, initialisation
      Notifications SmsNotificationService SMS reminders
      Access SsoRegistrationHandler User creation at single sign-on

      7.2 Triggers#

      Object Trigger Handler Events
      LoanApplication__c LoanApplicationTrigger LoanApplicationTriggerHandler before insert, before update, after update
      Lead LeadTrigger LeadTriggerHandler before insert

      7.2.1 Order of execution#

      On Lead, the trigger runs before save (score initialisation); the flow Lead_Assign_Branch runs after save (branch assignment). On LoanApplication__c, scoring happens before save, then the event is published and the archiving job is enqueued after update.

      7.3 Cross-cutting mechanisms#

      Loan status propagation. A single place detects status changes and publishes them; every consequence is a subscriber.

      7.4 Asynchronous and scheduled processing#

      Job Type Trigger or schedule Purpose
      CustomerSyncBatch Batch and Schedulable (batches of 50) Scheduled (schedule to be confirmed) Refresh the customer segment from the core banking system
      DocumentArchiveQueueable Queueable with callouts Status « Approved » or « Rejected » Archive the documents of the application
      SmsNotificationService.send @future with callout Invocable action of Loan_Document_Reminder Send the SMS reminders

      7.5 Flows#

      Flows handle simple record automation and scheduling; Apex handles scoring, integrations and volume.

      Flow Type Object Purpose
      Lead_Assign_Branch Record-triggered, after save, on create Lead Assign the branch of the lead
      Loan_Document_Reminder Scheduled, daily LoanApplication__c Remind customers of missing documents by SMS
      Loan_Status_Notification Platform event-triggered LoanStatusChange__e Create a follow-up task

      The full list is in Appendix B — Triggers and flows.

      7.6 OmniStudio#

      Component Type Role
      NWB_LoanIntake_English_1 OmniScript (NWB/LoanIntake) Guided loan intake; reuses the positionTile component to show the customer's positions
      NWB_GetPositions_English_1 Integration Procedure Server-side retrieval of positions (steps to be confirmed)
      NWB_ExtractLoan_1 Data Mapper (extract) Extraction of loan data (fields to be confirmed)

      7.7 Key sequences#

      Nightly customer synchronisation.

      8 User interface#

      8.1 Lightning apps and navigation#

      Both applications are Lightning consoles for desktop:

      • « Branch Console » (NWB_Branch_Console): customers, leads, loan applications, branches and the « New loan » tab; its home page is Branch_Home;
      • « Contact Center » (NWB_Contact_Center): leads, customers and contact attempts.

      8.2 Lightning pages#

      Page Object Custom components
      Account_Record_Page Account customer360
      Loan_Application_Record_Page LoanApplication__c loanTimeline
      Branch_Home Home page Standard components only

      8.3 Lightning Web Components#

      8.3.1 By domain#

      Domain Components Role
      Customer 360 customer360, positionTile Live positions of the customer
      Loans loanTimeline, loanWizard Timeline of an application; creation wizard in a tab

      8.4 Communication between components#

      • customer360 reads its data with a cached wire adapter on Customer360Controller and passes each position to positionTile as a public property.
      • loanTimeline uses Lightning Message Service; the channel LoanSelected is defined for selection events between components.
      • loanWizard uses the navigation service to open the created application.

      9 Integration architecture#

      9.1 Integration principles#

      • The core banking system remains the system of record: Salesforce reads positions live and stores only the keys and the segment.
      • Every outbound call uses a named credential; authentication is held by an external credential, never by code.
      • Calls from triggers and user transactions are asynchronous (queueable, @future); interactive reads are synchronous with an explicit timeout.
      • The inbound API creates records in user mode, with the permissions of the integration user.

      9.2 Integration patterns#

      Pattern Flows
      Remote Process Invocation — Request and Reply FLX-01 Customer positions
      Remote Process Invocation — Fire and Forget FLX-03 Document archiving, FLX-04 SMS reminders
      Batch Data Synchronization FLX-02 Nightly customer synchronisation
      Remote Call-In FLX-05 Lead creation from the mobile app

      SMS gateway Telecom partner sending SMS notifications NWB_SmsGateway
      Document store Long-term archive of the loan documents NWB_DocumentStore
      Corporate identity provider Single sign-on for employees (OpenID Connect) NWB_Corporate_IdP
      Mobile banking app Customer app that creates leads through the Salesforce API NWB_Mobile_Banking
      Maps provider Map tiles and geocoding shown in the branch console NWB_Map_Tiles, NWB_Maps

      9.4.1 Core banking#

      Read through NWB_CoreBanking, a secured endpoint whose authentication is held by the external credential NWB_CoreBanking_OAuth (OAuth, named principal). CoreBankingClient calls GET /customers/{number}/positions with a 10-second timeout, for the Customer 360 (FLX-01) and the customer synchronisation (FLX-02).

      9.4.2 Document store#

      DocumentArchiveQueueable posts the identifiers of decided applications to /archive through NWB_DocumentStore.

      9.4.3 SMS gateway#

      SmsNotificationService posts messages through NWB_SmsGateway, authenticated by the external credential NWB_SmsGateway_Key.

      9.4.4 Maps provider#

      Map tiles are allowed in the console by the CSP trusted site NWB_Map_Tiles; geocoding calls are allowed by the remote site NWB_Maps.

      9.5 Inbound APIs#

      URL mapping Apex class Nature
      /leads/v1/* LeadApiResource Apex REST

      The mobile banking app authenticates with the connected app NWB_Mobile_Banking (scopes Api and RefreshToken) and calls POST /services/apexrest/leads/v1/. The service creates a lead with the name, the channel and, when known, the customer number; the record is inserted with the permissions of the calling user.

      9.6 Authentication and single sign-on#

      Employees log in through the authentication provider NWB_Corporate_IdP (OpenID Connect). At first login, SsoRegistrationHandler creates the user from the identity provider claims and sets its federation identifier.

      9.7 Allowed domains#

      Kind API name Host
      Remote Site NWB_Maps maps.geo-provider.example
      CSP Trusted Site NWB_Map_Tiles tiles.geo-provider.example

      Both entries serve the maps provider: tiles in the Lightning pages (CSP) and server-side calls (remote site).

      10 Security and access#

      10.1 Principles#

      • Least privilege: a minimal profile, rights added by persona through permission set groups.
      • Record access follows the network: private defaults, opened by the role hierarchy and by targeted sharing rules.
      • Security is enforced on the server: with sharing, user-mode queries, inbound API in user mode.
      • No secret in code or configuration files: authentication is held by external credentials.

      10.2 Authentication and user provisioning#

      The assignment of permission set groups after creation is to be confirmed with the bank (manual or automated).

      10.3 Personas and permission set groups#

      Persona Permission set group Main rights
      Branch advisor NWB_Persona_Advisor NWB_Advisor: loan applications and contact attempts (create, edit), branches (read)
      Branch manager NWB_Persona_Branch_Manager NWB_Advisor and NWB_Branch_Manager: branches (edit)
      Contact center agent NWB_Persona_Agent NWB_Contact_Center_Agent: contact attempts

      Two technical permission sets complete the model: NWB_Integration_API (API access for the integration user) and NWB_Support_Admin (support administration).

      10.4 Role hierarchy#

      The hierarchy mirrors the network: chief executive, network director, regional directors, branch managers and advisors per region, and a separate branch for the contact center.

      10.5 Sharing model#

      10.5.1 Organization-wide defaults#

      Object Default sharing (internal / external)
      Account Private / Private
      Branch__c Read / Private
      ContactAttempt__c Private / Private
      Lead Private / Private
      LoanApplication__c Private / Private
      LoanDocument__c ControlledByParent / ControlledByParent
      Opportunity Private / Private

      Customers, leads, opportunities and loan applications are private; branches are readable by all; loan documents follow their application.

      10.5.2 Sharing rules and queues#

      Object Rule Kind Access
      LoanApplication__c Share_Submitted_With_Review_Team criteria Read
      API name Label Object
      Contact_Center_Leads Contact center leads Lead
      Loan_Review Loan review LoanApplication__c

      Submitted loan applications are opened in read-only mode to the group All_Branch_Managers, which includes the managers' superiors. Queues hold the work not yet assigned: loan applications to review and leads for the contact center.

      10.6 Application security#

      • 8 classes declare with sharing and 1 inherited sharing; the nightly synchronisation runs without sharing as a system job.
      • Queries from the Customer 360 and the selectors run WITH USER_MODE; the inbound API inserts as user.
      • Validation rules protect data consistency (Lead_Locked_When_Converted, Amount_Must_Be_Positive).

      10.7 Session settings and protections#

      Setting Value
      Session timeout Two hours, with forced logout
      Session locked to the domain Yes
      HttpOnly cookies Yes
      Password 12 characters minimum, upper and lower case, digits and special characters; expires after 90 days; locked after 5 attempts

      10.8 Integration users#

      The mobile banking app calls Salesforce as an integration user with the profile « NWB Integration » (Salesforce Integration licence) and the permission set NWB_Integration_API.

      11 Reporting and analytics#

      11.1 Reports and dashboards#

      Folder Count
      Loan_Reports 2

      The folder Loan_Reports holds the loan reports by status and by branch; the dashboard Loan_Pipeline presents the pipeline to branch managers. The branch home page embeds the dashboards.

      12 Environments, delivery and operations#

      12.1 Environments#

      The environments (sandboxes and their purpose) are to be confirmed with the bank. This document describes the production organization.

      12.2 Release management#

      The project is a Salesforce DX project (source format, API version 62.0). Metadata is deployed first, OmniStudio components second, then the active versions are checked. The pipeline and its approval gates are to be confirmed.

      12.3 Scheduled processing#

      Processing Frequency What to monitor
      CustomerSyncBatch Nightly (to be confirmed) Failed batches and records not updated (partial success)
      Loan_Document_Reminder Daily Flow errors, SMS gateway errors

      12.4 Logging and monitoring#

      Errors of asynchronous jobs are visible in the Apex jobs monitor and flow errors in the flow error e-mails. No specific logging framework is present in the metadata.

      12.5 Test strategy#

      5 test classes cover scoring, the trigger handler, the nightly batch and the inbound API. Callouts are isolated behind CoreBankingClient, which makes them mockable. Code coverage is to be read in the organization.

      13 Non-functional requirements#

      13.1 Measures per requirement#

      Requirement Measures in place
      Security Single sign-on, persona permission set groups, private defaults, user-mode queries, external credentials
      Performance Positions read on demand with a cached wire adapter; callouts with explicit timeouts
      Volume Nightly synchronisation in batches of 50 records; asynchronous archiving and SMS
      Availability Partial success on synchronisation; Customer 360 independent from the nightly job
      Maintainability Layered Apex, naming conventions, configuration in Custom Metadata
      Traceability Field history on specific objects, status change events

      13.2 Salesforce Well-Architected reading#

      Pillar Strengths observed
      Trusted Credentials outside the code, server-side security, least-privilege personas
      Easy Two task-oriented consoles, guided intake, live Customer 360
      Adaptable Event-driven follow-up, scoring by configuration, clear separation of layers

      14 Architecture decisions#

      ID Decision Rationale Consequence
      ADR-01 Read customer positions live from the core banking system Single source of truth, no duplication of financial data Customer 360 depends on the availability of the API
      ADR-02 Store the scoring rules in Custom Metadata Business changes without releases Rules are deployable and auditable like metadata
      ADR-03 Publish an event on each loan status change Add reactions without changing the trigger Subscribers run asynchronously
      ADR-04 Expose an Apex REST service for the mobile app Control of validation and defaults on the Salesforce side The service is versioned in its URL (/leads/v1/*)

      15 Outlook#

      • Extend the event-driven model to the contact center (notifications on lead assignment).
      • Enrich the loan intake journey with document upload.
      • Open a customer portal for loan follow-up.

      The detailed improvement register is kept in the companion Improvement Axes document.

      Appendix K — Glossary#

      Term Definition
      Branch Unit of the bank network that owns customers and leads by default (Branch__c).
      Custom Metadata Deployable configuration records, read by code and flows without consuming queries.
      External Credential Authentication definition (protocol, principals) used by named credentials.
      Flow Declarative automation of the Salesforce platform (record-triggered, scheduled, screen, autolaunched).
      loan application Request for a consumer loan or a mortgage, from intake to decision (LoanApplication__c).
      LWC Lightning Web Component: standards-based UI component of the Lightning platform.
      Named Credential Secure definition of a callout endpoint and its authentication.
      OWD Organization-Wide Defaults: baseline record access for each object.
      PSG Permission Set Group: bundle of permission sets assigned as one persona.
      Queue Shared owner for records awaiting assignment.
      Record Type Variant of an object with its own business process, picklist values and page layout.
